Compare leave-future-out evaluations across models

Source: R/lfo_cv.mvgam.R
loo_compare.mvgam_lfo.Rd

Ranks two or more lfo_cv() results by their summed ELPD, in the layout of loo::loo_compare(). The standard error of each difference comes from the paired per-fold differences with the best model. The results must share one evaluation grid, with the same min_t, fc_horizon and data.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mvgam_lfo'
loo_compare(x, ..., model_names = NULL)

Arguments

x

An mvgam_lfo object.

...

Further mvgam_lfo objects.

model_names

Optional character vector of model names, one per forecast. It replaces the names taken from the call.

Value

A compare.loo table in the layout of loo::loo_compare(), one row per model, best first.

model

The model's name.

elpd_diff

Summed ELPD difference from the best model, zero for the best.

se_diff

Standard error of elpd_diff, sqrt(N) * sd(fold_diff) over the N folds.

p_worse

The normal probability that the model forecasts worse than the best one (Sivula et al. 2025). NA for the best model and for a difference without spread.

diag_diff

"N < 100" for fewer than 100 folds, else "|elpd_diff| < 4" for a difference too small for its SE.

diag_elpd

The number of folds whose PSIS estimate was kept with a Pareto k above the threshold.

elpd_lfo

Summed per-fold ELPD.

se_elpd_lfo

Standard error of elpd_lfo.

References

Sivula, T., Magnusson, M., Matamoros, A. A. and Vehtari, A. (2025). Uncertainty in Bayesian leave-one-out cross-validation based model comparison. Bayesian Analysis. doi:10.1214/25-BA1569

See also

lfo_cv(), loo_model_weights.mvgam_lfo(), compare_elpds(), plot.mvgam_compare_elpds()

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(1)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                    n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())
# Two models of one count series: a smooth of x with and without
# an AR(1) trend. The trend model samples with smaller steps
# (adapt_delta = 0.95). That avoids divergent transitions when
# lfo_cv() refits it to shorter stretches of the series
mod_gam <- mvgam(y ~ s(x, k = 5), data = simdat$data_train,
                 family = poisson(), chains = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 209 of 2000 (10.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
mod_ar <- mvgam(y ~ s(x, k = 5), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
                data = simdat$data_train, family = poisson(),
                chains = 2, silent = 2,
                control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95))
#> Warning: 3 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
# }
# \dontrun{
# Each origin after t = 70 forecasts the next time step. The
# pointwise log densities feed stacking weights
lfo_gam <- lfo_cv(mod_gam, min_t = 70L, save_log_lik = TRUE)
#> Warning: 31 of 2000 (2.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
#> Warning: 14 of 2000 (1.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
#> Warning: 6 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
lfo_ar <- lfo_cv(mod_ar, min_t = 70L, save_log_lik = TRUE)
#> Warning: 3 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
#> Warning: 2 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# The model with the higher summed ELPD comes first
loo_compare(lfo_gam, lfo_ar, model_names = c("GAM", "AR"))
#>  model elpd_diff se_diff p_worse diag_diff diag_elpd
#>     AR       0.0     0.0      NA                    
#>    GAM     -36.5    12.3    1.00   N < 100          
#> 
#> Diagnostic flags present.
#> See ?`loo-glossary` (sections `diag_diff` and `diag_elpd`)
#> or https://mc-stan.org/loo/reference/loo-glossary.html.

# Next, compare_elpds() shows where along the series the models
# part ways
# }
